title: LiteResearcher: A Scalable Agentic RL Training Framework for Deep Research Agent

paper.title: LiteResearcher: A Scalable Agentic RL Training Framework for Deep Research Agent
paper.abstract: Abstract Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful training paradigm for LLM-based agents. However, scaling agentic RL for deep research remains constrained by two coupled challenges: hand-crafted synthetic data fails to elicit genuine real-world search capabilities, and real-world search dependency during RL training introduces instability and prohibitive cost, which limits the scalability of Agentic RL. LiteResearcher is a training framework that makes Agentic RL scalable: by constructing a lite virtual world that mirrors real-world search dynamics, we enable a continuously improving training recipe that empowers a tiny search agent to outperform large-scale open-source and commercial models (e.g., Tongyi DeepResearch and Claude-4.5 Sonnet). Specifically, on common benchmarks such as GAIA and Xbench, our LiteResearcher-4B achieves open-source state-of-the-art results of 71.3% and 78.0% respectively, demonstrating that scalable RL training is a key enabler for Deep Research Agents.

Figure 1: Performance of LiteResearcher. Left: Accuracy comparison on the Xbench DeepSearch benchmark across models of various scales. Right: Average rollout latency and cost per turn. 1 Introduction Recent advances in reinforcement learning (RL) on reasoning models ( Liu et al., 2025b ; Guo et al., 2025 ; Team et al., 2025a ) have demonstrated that continuously scaling model capabilities is achievable within stable training environments and with data of appropriate difficulty. However, when transitioning to agentic RL, where reasoning must be integrated with tool use, prior efforts have struggled to achieve similar sustained improvements. We identify the primary bottleneck as the inherent noise and instability of the real-world environment. In the domain of Coding Agents ( Wei et al., 2025b ; Jain et al., 2025 ) , this challenge has been effectively addressed through the use of isolated sandboxes configured to simulate production environments while filtering out infrastructure-level noise, thereby enabling scalable training. However, existing works in the domain of Deep Research have yet to realize such scalable RL training. Online RL frameworks ( Zheng et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025d ) interact directly with the live internet, introducing significant training variance and prohibitive costs that limit continuous capability growth. Local retrieval-based systems ( Jin et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025c ; Sun et al., 2025 ) are typically confined to a narrow corpus, making it impossible to replicate the complex search dynamics of the diverse internet. Meanwhile, current real-web graph-based data synthesis methods ( Jin et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025a ; Gao et al., 2025 ) rely on over-engineered reasoning structures, focusing on handcrafted logic while ignoring the diversity of atomic search techniques required for deep research, such as cross-verification and enumeration. We argue that scaling agentic RL for Deep Research requires a virtual world that mirrors the structure of the live internet but is isolated in execution: the twin architecture ensures that policies optimized in the virtual environment can generalize to the open web, while isolation shields the training process from the high variance and stochasticity of environmental noise. In this paper, we present LiteResearcher , an Agentic RL training framework designed to construct a virtual world that mirrors real-world web architecture . We follow these steps to realize the scaling potential of agentic RL: (1) Synthesize real search data; (2) Simulate search environment; (3) Achieve sustained improvements through curriculum RL. The foundation of this virtual world is generating realistic training tasks. To capture the diversity of information seeking in real-world user queries, we prioritize the scale of information sources in our virtual world. We find that by scaling up information sources, even a simple-but-effective data synthesis can yield a realistic distribution of training tasks. Crucially, handling these synthetic tasks requires a corresponding execution environment. We simulate a realistic search environment by enriching our corpus with these tasks. For every synthetic task, we perform a targeted expansion of the local webpage corpus by searching and fetching related real-world webpages, which then construct the local search and browse tool. This ensures that for any given training task, the local search and browse tools provide search dynamics analogous to the open web, allowing the agent to obtain real-web atom capabilities in a controlled environment. Even with synthetic tasks and tools, training can still saturate if the model gets trapped at a certain difficulty threshold, correctly solving easy tasks while completely failing complex ones. We apply a difficulty-aware curriculum RL which progressively enhances both task difficulty and context length across training stages. At each stage, we only keep the synthetic tasks that the current model can partially solve, discarding both trivially easy and impossibly hard instances, thereby providing consistent training signal for improvement. Our tiny search agent LiteResearcher-4B achieves 71.3% on GAIA ( Mialon et al., 2023 ) and 78.0% on Xbench ( Chen et al., 2025 ) , surpassing open-source agents up to 8 × 8\times larger such as Tongyi DeepResearch 30B (70.9%/75.0%) and WebSailor 30B (53.2%/53.3%), while matching or exceeding proprietary systems including Claude-4.5-Sonnet (71.2%/66.0%) and GLM-4.6 (71.9%/70.0%). These results demonstrate that scalable RL can yield a powerful on-device deep research agent. 2 Related Work Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning The pursuit of advanced reasoning in LLMs initially relied on inference-time heuristics such as Chain-of-Thought prompting ( Wei et al., 2022 ) and Tree of Thoughts ( Yao et al., 2023 ) . A paradigm shift occurred with the demonstration that RL can internalize reasoning capabilities directly into model weights. DeepSeek-R1 ( Guo et al., 2025 ) showed that RL with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is sufficient to unlock emergent reasoning behaviors such as self-verification and backtracking, and subsequent work has rapidly advanced optimization ( Yu et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2025b ) , reward design ( Cui et al., 2025 ) , and scaling ( Hu et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2025 ) , establishing RLVR as a general-purpose post-training paradigm. However, all these methods operate as closed-world reasoners: they rely solely on parametric knowledge and lack the ability to interact with external dynamic environments—a critical limitation for tasks requiring real-time information retrieval. Agentic Deep Research Models Recent research has pivoted towards Agentic Deep Research, where agents interact with external search environments through iterative query formulation and page navigation. This line of work can be grouped by environment design. Online real-world RL systems ( Zheng et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025d ; Li et al., 2025a ) train directly on the live web, offering realistic interactions but incurring high cost and non-deterministic reward signals. Local retrieval-based systems ( Jin et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025c ; Gao et al., 2025 ) construct environments from Wikipedia or similar corpora, providing fast, deterministic interactions but remaining confined to narrow, homogeneous domains. Simulated systems such as ZeroSearch ( Sun et al., 2025 ) replace search engines by training an LLM to mimic search engine outputs, but sacrifice page-level fidelity. Recent lightweight explorations such as AgentCPM-Explore ( Chen et al., 2026 ) further show the capability of small deep-research agents, but still fail to realize scalable RL training. In contrast, our framework builds a local environment with real-world data and a search engine, enabling scalable RL training. 3 Preliminaries: Agentic Framework We model deep research as a sequential decision-making process under the ReAct framework ( Yao et al., 2022 ) . Given an initial user query q q , the agent interacts with the environment over multiple steps by alternately generating reasoning thoughts, executing actions, and receiving observations. The history up to step t t is denoted by ℋ t = ( q , τ 1 , a 1 , o 1 , … , τ t , a t , o t ) , \mathcal{H}_{t}=(q,\tau_{1},a_{1},o_{1},\dots,\tau_{t},a_{t},o_{t}), where τ i \tau_{i} , a i a_{i} , and o i o_{i} denote the thought, action, and environmental observation at step i i , respectively. At each step, the agent first generates a reasoning thought τ t \tau_{t} conditioned on the preceding history, and then selects an executable action a t a_{t} conditioned on both ℋ t − 1 \mathcal{H}_{t-1} and τ t \tau_{t} : τ t ∼ π θ ( ⋅ ∣ ℋ t − 1 ) , a t ∼ π θ ( ⋅ ∣ ℋ t − 1 , τ t ) . \tau_{t}\sim\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid\mathcal{H}_{t-1}),\qquad a_{t}\sim\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid\mathcal{H}_{t-1},\tau_{t}). Action Space. The action space 𝒜 \mathcal{A} consists of two primitive actions: • Search ( q ′ ) (q^{\prime}) : submits a natural-language query q ′ q^{\prime} to the search engine and returns a ranked list of retrieved snippets and URLs. • Browse ( u , q ′ ) (u,q^{\prime}) : visits a selected URL u u and returns a query-conditioned summary of the page content. After collecting sufficient information, the agent terminates environment interaction and generates a final response to the original user query q q . 4 Methods: Towards Scalable Training To explore the scaling potential of Agentic Deep Research, we aim to establish a scalable training framework as a mandatory first step. Current paradigms that rely on high-latency, unstable online interactions fundamentally bottleneck this process. In this section, we present our LiteResearcher framework, which decouples agent evolution from the open web while ensuring generalization to real-world web dynamics. As illustrated in Figure 2 , the ecosystem is built upon three core pillars: (1) Co-construct Training Data and Corpus Pipeline : To achieve diversity in the data distribution and scalability in data quantity, we propose a unified framework that co-evolves the training data and the local corpus. (2) Stable Local Tool Environment : Leveraging the enriched webpage corpus, we construct a Local Search Engine and Local Browse Tool that mirror the behavior of real-world search dynamics within the synthesized data. (3) Difficulty-Aware Curriculum Learning : To continuously expand the model’s capability boundaries, we leverage our unlimited synthetic data pool to implement a multi-stage curriculum that serves the model with data of appropriate difficulty, thereby ensuring sustainable performance improvements. Figure 2: System architecture overview. (a) Corpus Extension and QA Synthesis : An iterative data engine which also enriches local webpage corpus, powering stable, local tools for zero-cost agent RL training. (b) Reinforcement Curriculum Learning : Synthetic tasks are leveled by complexity to guide the agent through progressive training stages.
